$comment: Provider pool template schema (src/providers/<name>/connector.json, and every pool a provider.mjs returns). Every per-CLI quirk lives HERE, never in core logic. See docs/reference/providers.md.
name: pool name: the provider name, or <provider>:<suffix> for extra pools a provider returns
bin: binary on PATH to probe for discovery

spawn.$comment: argv template; {taskFile} {cwd} {sessionId} {bullswarmDir} are substituted ({bullswarmDir} is the package root)
spawn.$comment-cwd: cwdMode documents how the CLI resolves its project: 'pwd' means the CLI resolves from $PWD so the watcher MUST set PWD and spawn inside --add-dir

conversation.$comment: Optional session arguments. followUp is a connector-owned one-turn recovery command; the watcher substitutes {sessionId}, {prompt}, {cwd}, {taskFile}, and {bullswarmDir}, then appends eventStreamArgs verbatim (or eventStream.args when followUp omits it).
newArgs: optional arguments for a new session, with {sessionId}
resumeArgs: optional arguments for a resumed normal attempt, with {sessionId}

followUp.$comment: The command is spawned directly (no shell), so {prompt} is one argv element even when it contains spaces. The watcher runs at most one follow-up after a detected truncated response.

authSignatures: strings in output that mean auth/throttle failure
quotaSignatures: strings in output that mean this credential's usage window is spent RIGHT NOW (session/weekly/monthly limit hit)
$comment-quotaSignatures: Optional. Spent-window wording. Merged on top of DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIGNATURES (src/lib/quota.js), matched case-insensitively, and only honored when the matched line is quota-shaped (<=300 chars and the phrase starts in the first 40 chars or the line is error-shaped) so agent prose and tool output that merely discuss limits are never killed. A hit is a limit notice (checked before authSignatures) and kills the attempt; it pauses the pool only on proof (decideQuotaPause, doctrine Q6): the notice names its reset (paused until that reset) or the pool's own meter reads >= 95% on a running window (paused until that window resets). Without proof it is a transient throttle: retried, never a pause. A phrase core knows as throttle wording stays a throttle even when listed here.
throttleSignatures: strings in output that mean a momentary request throttle (please wait a moment and try again)
$comment-throttleSignatures: Optional. Transient-throttle wording, merged on top of DEFAULT_THROTTLE_SIGNATURES (src/lib/quota.js) under the same quota-shaped gate. A throttle is NOT a spent window: the attempt is retried on the same pool after a short backoff (THROTTLE_BACKOFF_MS) and the pool is never paused. A named wait longer than THROTTLE_MAX_WAIT_MS (15 minutes) skips the same-pool retry and moves the attempt to another pool, still without a pause. Only the Q6 proof (a spent window with its reset named, or the pool's meter >= 95%) pauses a pool.

outputExtraction.$comment: how to get the real answer out of stdout+stderr+files
outputExtraction.field: optional json field path or file glob

eventStream.$comment: Optional declarative JSONL adapter. Provider quirks stay here; core emits normalized semantic actions.
args: CLI flags that enable machine-readable streaming
modelPaths: provider model-id paths in priority order
eventStream.$comment-toolKinds: Optional. How this provider's tool names map to the kinds the Step page counts: command (a shell command), read (a file's contents), edit (a write, edit or patch), search (grep, glob, a directory listing or a web search), other. A key is the tool name the connector captures as the event kind (its kindPaths value), matched case-insensitively; a name the map does not list counts as other and is named on the turn row. Every provider owns its own vocabulary here; src/workflow/step-model.js keeps no table of tool names.

idPaths: provider action id paths in priority order
eventIdPaths: optional provider event-id paths; omitted when the provider supplies none
rules.$comment-optional-match: Each optional field may add <field>Match to restrict mapping to a provider context; absent matches map whenever its paths resolve.

usagePaths.cumulative: true when the mapped values are cumulative

usage.$comment: Optional provider-reported token/cost totals. mode=last for a cumulative final event, sum for per-request events, max for monotonic counters.

fields.cacheWrite: provider aggregate or single cache-write path

inclusive.$comment: Optional. Each parent counter includes the listed component counters; the decoder subtracts them and floors at zero.

eventStream.$comment-capture: Optional. Core defaults (src/lib/attempt-stream.js): responseBytes 64000, fileBytes 1048576. Applied when the block is omitted, so a contributed connector needs no code to take part. Both fields are optional positive integers.

meter.$comment: none | declared (manual) | reader (programmatic: the owning provider exports readUsage)

modelDiscovery.$comment: Optional local CLI model listing. Parsing quirks stay connector-owned. A provider.mjs discoverModels export may instead name a provider-owned protocol and use timeoutMs; knownModels is only the failure fallback.

$comment-modelFamilies: Optional. A family rule gives every model whose id matches `match` (a regex, tested without a trailing [1m]-style selector) its tier and base qualityRank; within one family the higher version read from the id always ranks first. The version is the first standalone digit run (gpt-5.6-sol -> 5.6, claude-opus-5-5 -> 5.5), or the named capture group `version` when the pattern has one. No pricing, benchmark, or free here: those are one model's facts and belong on an exact modelProfiles row, which may also override a family's tier, rank, or autoRecommend.
$comment-generationFallback: Optional, per tier. When the family serving an opted-in tier has no model in the pool's newest generation (the highest leading version number among its recommendable family members), the tier takes the newest-generation model of the next-lower-ranked family at `reasoning` (clamped to what that model supports). An opted-in tier that no family serves and no model is ranked for (a provider with one model line) takes the best-ranked family's newest-generation model the same way. `label` names a generation in the explanation, e.g. gpt-{generation} -> 'no gpt-6 terra yet'; an optional `why` replaces the generated explanation.

low.why: optional plain reason shown with the suggestion

reasoning.$comment: Optional. How THIS CLI expresses a thinking level. Omit the block entirely when the CLI has no such control: core then appends nothing and reports source 'unsupported'. Declare exactly one of flag/args.
reasoning.$comment-form: flag: appended as `<flag> <level>` with replace-or-append semantics, so a level already pinned in spawn.cmd is replaced rather than duplicated. args: appended verbatim with {level} substituted, for CLIs whose control is a config override rather than a flag.
reasoning.$comment-levels: the subset of the common scale (low, medium, high, xhigh, max — weakest to strongest, src/lib/reasoning.js) that this CLI accepts, weakest first. A requested level outside the subset is clamped to the strongest supported level not above it, or to the weakest supported level when the request is below all of them, and the clamp is recorded.
reasoning.$comment-defaults: the level to use for each effort tier when nothing else asked. Last layer of the precedence chain: action override > run override > strategy per-pool > strategy per-tier > THESE > nothing appended. The literal 'default' at any layer means 'append nothing, let the CLI's own configuration decide'.
reasoning.$comment-skipModels: Optional connector-owned regexes. A selected model matching one gets no level appended (source 'skipped-model'), for CLIs whose flag is only valid on some models.

$comment-reasoning: Optional prose companion. Say which command's output the block was read from, and mark anything the CLI does not actually print as UNVERIFIED — never invent an accepted value.
$comment-readTranscriptUsage: Optional provider.mjs hook: readTranscriptUsage({ provider, sessionId = null, cwd = null, startedAt = null, endedAt = null, home }) returns provider-summed token classes and its confidence; see docs/reference/providers.md.
credentialGroup: optional shared-credential group id, e.g. relay:relay.example
$comment-credentialGroup: Pools with the same credentialGroup share one upstream credential: an auth failure on one benches its siblings and dispatch avoids retrying the group. `upstreamGroup` is the accepted legacy spelling of this field.

flags.$comment-stealth: stealth=true: prompts/completions retained by an anonymous provider — opt-in only, never a default

$comment-timeout: Delegates have no implicit wall-clock timeout; use direct --timeout or workflow step.timeoutSec as an explicit opt-in
